reason: Verification flagged critical logic flaws (day-ordering and inventory-gated wearing) that materially distort outcomes, along with performance and completeness gaps. We are at iteration 0 of 3, leaving ample room to correct these and substantially improve correctness, scalability, and metric coverage in the next pass.

specific_areas: Reorder daily loop: policy -> info -> behavior -> mobility/enforcement -> retail -> aggregation; treat observation/enforcement as lagged signals for next day.
Gate mask wearing on actual inventory or immediate household allocation; generate purchase intents for future days only.
Deduct fines from household budgets during enforcement and record in events.
Introduce and use persistent id_to_agent and person_id_to_household maps; remove linear next(...) lookups.
Honor locations_count_by_type parameter; remove dead/duplicate household creation; align person SES with household SES.
Compute missing metrics: peak_adoption and sustained_adoption_post_mandate; include in evaluation outputs.
Harden error handling (avoid StopIteration without defaults), remove unused variables, and clean redundant code.
Pass previous-day avg_price into behavior decisions; ensure last_observed_compliance updates after mobility for use next day.
Add unit tests for day-ordering, inventory gating, and fine deduction; add a micro-benchmark or lint check for O(N) lookups in hot loops.
